name: Aetius of Antioch
otherNames: Atheus, "the godless", a name Socrates and Sozomen report and Athanasius uses
knownFor: A bold Arian logician who taught that the Son is unlike the Father, founding the Anomoean party; his own allies gave him up in 360.
dates: Active from about 350; died at Constantinople after 366
place: From Coele-Syria; taught at Antioch and Alexandria

keyWorks.title: The Syntagmation
keyWorks.about: a short book of logical propositions arguing the Son is unlike the Father, kept inside Epiphanius's Panarion 76, which copies it out to refute it

traces: The Anomoeans, later called Eunomians after his pupil Eunomius of Cyzicus, who carried his teaching on.
remembered: Sozomen says he reasoned so boldly about God that many people called him Atheus, the godless one.
At the Council of Constantinople in 360 his friend Eudoxius, then bishop of Antioch, gave him up, and the council took away his office of deacon.

uncertain: His life is told mostly through partisans. Philostorgius, who praised him, gives the story of the poor goldsmith who rose by logic; his history survives only in a hostile summary by Photius. Socrates, Sozomen and Epiphanius, who opposed him, tell the rest.

Socrates of Constantinople, a hostile witness, says he leaned on Aristotle's Categories and framed arguments that deceived himself, and that his fellow Arians pronounced him a heretic. Philostorgius praised the force of his arguments.
The years of his birth and death are not given in a held source. Philostorgius places his death at Constantinople, after the revolt of Procopius and after Julian had given him land on Lesbos.
